judges.name: Judge Tool-Permission Argv Collapse Judge
judges.invariant: A judge round argv MUST always carry explicit tool restriction flags and must not omit them when requested tools contain no read-only tools.
judges.tested_scenario: Stage manifest specifies verify judge with allowedTools: ['Write', 'Bash'] or allowedTools: []
judges.physical_result: AgentInvocationOptions.renderForJudge filters requested tools against JUDGE_READ_ONLY_TOOLS (['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob']). When the intersection is empty, effectiveJudgeAllowedTools returns an empty list. addToolListFlag omits the --allowedTools flag entirely if tools are empty. The resulting argv is ['--model', '<model>'] with NO --allowedTools parameter.
judges.runtime_exploitability: UNVERIFIED (live nested provider invocation restricted by Teamwork anti-recursion harness; actual tool authorization depends on vendor CLI default permission mode in non-interactive print mode)

judges.name: FreshJudgeEnvironments Shared Container Judge
judges.invariant: Multi-vote quorum environments must maintain isolation if execution environments permit mutation.
judges.tested_scenario: Multiple judge votes executed sequentially for the same attempt commit SHA
judges.physical_result: FreshJudgeEnvironments reuses the exact same container instance for all votes of an attempt: 'if (current != null && sha.equals(currentSha)) return current;'. If an earlier vote performs filesystem mutations (conditional on ARGV gap exploitability), subsequent votes execute in the contaminated container.

judges.name: JudgeVerdictExtractor Code-Fence Desynchronization & Pass-Smuggling Judge
judges.invariant: The final verdict extracted from the judge model MUST correspond to the model's actual terminal evaluation and must not be fooled by illustrative snippets in preceding commentary.
judges.tested_scenario: Judge model response quotes a mock configuration with {'passed': true} in an early code block, followed by analysis and a terminal verdict {'passed': false, 'findings': ['...']}
judges.physical_result: JudgePromptBuilder instructs the model: 'End your final message with a JSON object...'. However, JudgeVerdictExtractor uses FENCE.matcher(text).find() to match the FIRST code fence in the text, and scans for the FIRST balanced '{...}' block. When the model includes preliminary code examples or mock JSON objects before its final verdict, the extractor parses the preliminary block. If that block contains 'passed: true', the round is recorded as Verdict.Pass(), silently ignoring the real failure and advancing unverified work into production.

judges.name: JudgeVerdictExtractor Non-JSON Code Fence CannotVerify Taint Judge
judges.invariant: A model that correctly identifies a quality failure but cites code snippets should fail the attempt, not trigger an unburned infrastructure escalation.
judges.tested_scenario: Judge quotes Java/C/Rust method containing braces in a code block before its final JSON verdict fence
judges.physical_result: The extractor captures the first fence containing Java/C/Rust code with braces, attempts to parse it via Jackson ObjectMapper, fails with JsonParseException, and returns Verdict.CannotVerify. In JudgeVoting, a single CannotVerify immediately short-circuits the voting loop and escalates without burning an attempt, converting legitimate quality failures into infrastructure outages.
